To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“Language-derived estimates of personality and demographics can accurately distinguish users that tweet about mental illness from controls.

(i) language-derived personality and demographic features are useful in identifying Twitter users that disclose a diagnosis of depression and PTSD, and that (ii) language use of users that disclose a mental illness is similar to the language use of those that do not disclose.

we can predict whether a person is likely to have a mental illness from their Twitter profile with a high degree of accuracy and that the language they use on social media is a good indicator of their symptoms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the language use of people who disclose mental illness, with an emphasis on depression and PTSD, and how this relates to their demographics and personality traits.
the use of Twitter to understand the language use of people who self-identify with depression or PTSD.

the use of language to characterise mental illness on social media, which has the potential to help identify those at risk and to provide a better understanding of how mental illnesses affect people in everyday life.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the language of users who self-disclose depression or PTSD is significantly different from that of random controls.
personality and demographics are strong signals for the mental illness status of a Twitter user.

the personality, age, gender and language use of Twitter users who disclose mental illness are highly predictive of the mental illness they disclose, and the language they use is consistent with the symptoms associated with their mental illness in clinical literature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the language use of Twitter users disclosing a mental illness can be used to estimate their personality and demographics with high precision, and can be used to recover symptoms associated with mental illnesses.

the personality and demographic estimates we obtain from language use are strong predictors of mental illness, and the language of users disclosing mental illness is consistent with the clinical literature.

, in the case of Twitter users disclosing depression or PTSD, personality, age, gender, and symptoms can be estimated reliably from the language they use, and that this can be used as an early indicator of risk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the language of users on Twitter can be used to identify users with mental illness, as well as their symptoms, even when they are not explicitly disclosing a diagnosis.

the language use of people tweeting about their mental illnesses is highly informative of their personality, age, gender, and symptoms, and that these features are useful for distinguishing users with different mental health problems.
, in addition to being useful for mental health research, the language of social media can be used to identify and support people in need.
